zh.metaDescription: DMC2601946 · 多约束货物运输装箱与多车型决策项目经历，展示三维装箱、层模板组合、Pareto 筛选、动态规划与剪枝搜索能力。

blocks.text: 完整竞赛论文（92 页）可通过以下链接查看或下载。

rows: 项目
题目
“箱”尽其用——多约束下货物运输装箱的分层组合优化与多车型决策
状态
结果待公布
项目类型
数学建模项目经历
个人角色
核心建模负责人；辅助编程与论文写作

blocks.text: 该项目围绕多场景、多目标货物运输装箱策略优化问题，综合考虑货物姿态限制、堆叠支撑关系、易碎件特殊承托要求、局部承压上限、顶部安全间隙、车型选择与跨车分配等实际运输约束，建立三维装箱优化与多车型组合决策模型。
题目要求在两种标准车型和五类货物条件下，分别求解单车型装箱方案与多车型组合运输方案。模型需要在全部货物可运输、货物不得重叠、姿态合法、支撑稳定、易碎件安全承托、局部承压不超限、顶部预留安全间隙等约束下，优化空间利用率、载重利用率、车辆数量和运输成本。

blocks.alt: 标准件、易碎件和定向件三类货物示意图
blocks.caption: 图：三类货物约束对象示意，包括标准件、易碎件和定向件，为后续姿态限制、支撑关系与易碎件封顶约束建模提供基础。

blocks.text: 针对四个问题，我们构建了一套多任务协同的数学模型体系，涵盖时序回归、行为转化预测、在线状态判别和分时段动态推荐四大模块。

blocks.caption: 核心建模模块
rows: 三维装箱约束建模
三维坐标系 + 姿态变量 + 空间位置变量
描述标准件、易碎件、定向件的合法姿态、空间占据和边界约束
支撑与承压建模
支撑父节点集合、有效支撑域、接触面积分担
检验货物稳定性、易碎件完整承托和局部压强上限
单车型求解
层模板构造—层序组合优化 + 网格搜索
将三维装箱拆解为二维铺排与一维堆叠，降低搜索复杂度
多车型组合优化
车辆启用、车型选择、货物跨车分配
分别以总车辆数最少和总运输成本最低为目标求解运输方案
模板库压缩
混合层模板枚举 + Pareto 非支配筛选
保留层高不增大且货物件数更优的候选模板，压缩搜索空间
组合求解与验证
二维动态规划精确覆盖 + 高度剪枝、支撑闭合剪枝、分布剪枝
恢复最优模板组合，并逐车验证装载可行性

blocks.caption: 求解结果摘要
rows: 单独选用车型 1
需 18 辆车，空间利用率 96.5%，载重利用率 52.6%
单独选用车型 2
需 8 辆车，空间利用率 96.3%，载重利用率 74.2%
多车型组合优化
总车辆数最少与总成本最低两个目标下，最优方案均为 8 辆车型 2
运输成本
总运输成本 5600 元，未使用车型 1
承压校核
最大局部压强 319 kg/m²，低于 500 kg/m² 承压上限
灵敏度分析
顶部安全间隙在 3 cm 附近模型较稳定；超过 10 cm 后装载性能显著下降

blocks.alt: 车型 2 最优装箱方案三维可视化
blocks.caption: 图：单独选用车型 2 的最优装配方案样例，空间利用率为 96.3%，载重利用率为 74.2%。

blocks.alt: 顶部安全间隙灵敏度分析结果
blocks.caption: 图：顶部安全间隙对空间利用率、载重利用率、装载高度和层数的影响，用于检验模型在安全裕度变化下的稳定性。

blocks.alt: 局部承压热力图可行性验证
blocks.caption: 图：局部承压热力图验证装载方案的稳定性，最大局部压强低于题设承压上限。

blocks.text: 我负责该作品的全部核心建模工作，包括三维装箱约束体系设计、货物姿态集合定义、支撑关系与局部承压建模、层模板构造、混合层组合优化、Pareto 筛选逻辑、动态规划与剪枝求解思路设计，并辅助完成程序实现、结果可视化和论文写作。

en.metaDescription: DMC2601946 · Cargo packing and multi-vehicle decision-making project, demonstrating 3D packing, layer-template optimization, Pareto filtering, dynamic programming, and pruning search.

blocks.text: The full competition paper (92 pages) is available for viewing or downloading.

rows: Project
DMC2601946 · Problem D
Title
Hierarchical Combinatorial Optimization and Multi-vehicle Decision-making for Cargo Packing under Multiple Constraints
Status
Result pending
Project Type
Mathematical modeling project experience
Role
Lead modeler; assisted with programming and paper writing

blocks.text: This project addresses a multi-scenario and multi-objective cargo packing problem. It incorporates practical transportation constraints such as cargo orientation, stacking support, fragile-item support, local pressure limits, top safety clearance, vehicle-type selection, and cross-vehicle allocation.

The task required solving both single-vehicle packing and mixed-vehicle transportation planning under two standard vehicle types and five cargo categories. The model had to satisfy non-overlap, legal orientation, support stability, fragile-item protection, local pressure limits, top clearance, and complete transportation constraints while optimizing volume utilization, weight utilization, truck count, and transportation cost.

blocks.alt: Illustration of standard, fragile, and orientation-constrained cargo types
blocks.caption: Figure: Three cargo categories considered in the model, including standard items, fragile items, and orientation-constrained items. These categories define the basis for orientation, support, and top-layer constraints.

blocks.text: We constructed a multi-task collaborative mathematical model system covering four modules: time-series regression, behavior conversion prediction, online status classification, and time-slot dynamic recommendation.

blocks.caption: Core Modeling Modules
rows: 3D packing constraints
3D coordinate system, orientation variables, and position variables
Describes legal orientations, occupied space, and boundary constraints for standard, fragile, and directional items
Support and pressure model
Parent support sets, effective support regions, and contact-area load allocation
Checks stability, full support for fragile items, and local pressure limits
Single-vehicle solution
Layer-template construction and layer-sequence optimization with grid search
Decomposes 3D packing into 2D layout and 1D stacking to reduce search complexity
Multi-vehicle optimization
Vehicle activation, type selection, and cross-vehicle cargo allocation
Solves minimum-truck and minimum-cost transportation plans
Template compression
Mixed-layer enumeration and Pareto non-dominated filtering
Keeps high-quality layer candidates and reduces the search space
Optimization and verification
2D dynamic programming exact coverage plus height, support-closure, and distribution pruning
Recovers optimal layer combinations and verifies feasibility for each truck

blocks.caption: Result Summary
rows: Type-1 vehicle only
18 trucks required, with 96.5% volume utilization and 52.6% weight utilization
Type-2 vehicle only
8 trucks required, with 96.3% volume utilization and 74.2% weight utilization
Mixed-vehicle optimization
Both minimum-truck and minimum-cost objectives selected 8 type-2 vehicles
Transportation cost
Total cost was 5600 RMB, with no type-1 vehicle used
Pressure validation
Maximum local pressure was 319 kg/m², below the 500 kg/m² limit
Sensitivity analysis
The model was stable near the 3 cm top-clearance baseline; performance declined significantly beyond 10 cm

blocks.alt: 3D visualization of the optimal packing plan for vehicle type 2
blocks.caption: Figure: Optimal packing example for vehicle type 2, with 96.3% volume utilization and 74.2% weight utilization.

blocks.alt: Sensitivity analysis of top safety clearance
blocks.caption: Figure: Sensitivity analysis of top safety clearance, showing its influence on volume utilization, weight utilization, loaded height, and number of layers.

blocks.alt: Local pressure heatmap for feasibility verification
blocks.caption: Figure: Local pressure heatmap used to verify packing feasibility and structural stability under the pressure limit.

blocks.text: I was responsible for all core modeling work, including the 3D packing constraint system, orientation-set definition, support and local pressure modeling, layer-template construction, mixed-layer combinatorial optimization, Pareto filtering logic, and the dynamic-programming and pruning-based solution framework. I also assisted with implementation, visualization, and paper writing.
